title: Keeping Time on the Ride
description: Swap the hi-hat for the ride cymbal and hear how it changes the mood of a beat.

steps.title: Meet the ride
steps.description: The ride is the big cymbal off to the drummer's side. It does the same job as the hi-hat, keeping a steady pulse, but it sounds more open: a clear "ping" with a wash of shimmer underneath. Jazz drummers live on it. Rock drummers often move over to it for a chorus or a bridge, when they want things to breathe a bit more.

steps.title: Hit the ride
steps.description: Hit the ride and let it ring. Notice how it keeps humming after the ping.
steps.hint: It's in the bottom right corner, labelled RDE.

steps.title: Ride and kick
steps.description: Hit the ride and kick together. A soft kick under the ride is where a lot of jazz grooves start.
steps.hint: KCK is top left and RDE is bottom right, so you're reaching corner to corner.

steps.title: Ride and snare
steps.description: Now the ride with the snare. This is your backbeat, beats 2 and 4, with the ride keeping time instead of the hi-hat.
steps.hint: Snare (SNR) on the top row, ride (RDE) in the bottom right.

steps.title: All three
steps.description: Kick, snare and ride together. Compare it in your head with the hi-hat version. Same beat, but it feels bigger and looser.
steps.hint: Kick and snare are side by side at the top left, and the ride is bottom right. Close together in time is enough.

steps.title: Where you'll hear it
steps.description: Which style leans on the ride cymbal the most to keep time?
